entries.test: Public tests of contemporaneous OpenAI LLMs would establish whether they routinely fabricate information when used to retrieve stored facts.
entries.note: “Lousy databases” has a plain factual reading here: unreliable factual retrieval because of hallucinations.

entries.test: Public evaluations of the original GPT-4 on reasoning tasks with supplied facts would show how frequently its conclusions are invalid.
entries.note: The stated definition makes the claim testable despite the unspecified frequency threshold.
Whether a mechanism counts as “really reasoning” lacks a shared empirical test. Producing valid conclusions would not by itself settle this categorical distinction.

entries.test: Microsoft's contemporaneous public responsible-AI commitments and documented responsibilities after the team layoff would establish whether its actions contradicted those commitments.
entries.note: Marcus asserts a contradiction, but the website statement referenced by “this” is absent from the supplied text. The specific commitment attributed by the proposition therefore cannot be verified from this record.

entries.test: OpenAI's public warnings, model disclosures, and documented mitigations available by March 18, 2023 would show whether any warned-of harm had been solved and whether any model workings had been disclosed.
entries.note: These are categorical assertions about the situation at publication. Partial mitigation alone would not establish that a harm was solved.
